_comment: laneAM different-unit gap sub-range fills at margin T=1. Every entry is BYTE-TRUE, but note objdiff's report driver sets function_reloc_diffs=None, so 'byte-true' here means IDENTICAL MODULO EVERY RELOCATION TARGET -- two funclets with the same instruction bytes but different callees and different string/data references score a true 100%. What is NOT established is WHICH unit owns each entry. Attribution is pairwise only: it discriminates the left neighbour from the right and cannot exclude a third owner. Two independent measurements say the same thing: (a) a held-out control assigning gaps to a random CERTAINLY-WRONG unit still scored 36.7% of functions (57.1% at 17-32 bytes), and 95.1% of this yield is 17-44 bytes; (b) a validated static signature predictor (547/547 vs objdiff-cli) finds the median LEFT_ONLY signature occurs in 122 of our 1,024 objs -- only 128 of 1,531 evidenced functions have a signature unique to one unit tree-wide. TREAT ALL ENTRIES AS UNIT-ATTRIBUTION-UNRESOLVED, same doctrine as _icf_arbitrary and _bijection_arbitrary. The identity_unresolved tier is stronger still: those matched under EITHER neighbour and are pure coin flips. Evidence: docs/plans/lane-am-diffunit-2026-07-26.md.
